item.title: Kevin Durant's night vs. Suns: A milestone, a clash with Dillon Brooks and a win for Rockets
item.description: Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant (7) and Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks (3) argue on the court during the second half of an NBA Cup basketball game, Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, in Houston. (AP Photo/Karen Warren) (AP Photo/Karen Warren) Kevin Durant scored his 33,000th career point Wednesday and spent a chunk of a late-game possession - with the Houston Rockets' 116-104 win over the Phoenix Suns all-but secured - jawing with former Rockets forward Dillon Brooks. The two got in each other's faces as the game wound down, a heated discussion that ended with both players earning technical fouls - Brooks' was his second of the game, leading to an automatic ejection. KD and Dillon Brooks going at each other https://t.co/r1tQ9nb9cN - Erik Ruby (@ErikRuby) November 26, 2026 "I don't mind if somebody got a grievance with me. I don't mind addressing it right there in the moment. I'm sure (Brooks) has some," said Durant, who scored 20 points. "I said some things he probably didn't like, and he addressed it right there and I respect that as a man. It didn't get further than that. "But if it does get further than that, I'll be ready for that too." Durant wasn't the only Rocket to trash talk with Brooks, who popped into Houston's locker room after the Suns beat the Rockets in Phoenix on Nov. 5 but didn't do so after the loss at Toyota Center. Brooks, one of the players Houston traded for Durant, also got into it with former teammates Amen Thompson, Fred VanVleet and Alperen Şengün. "It's going to be that every night with (Brooks). We know that and for good or bad, it can help your team or hinder your team at times," said coach Ime Udoka said. "I think our guys did a good job of keeping it cool, playing through it, although quite a few guys got technicals." Houston led by just three with under five minutes left but went 6-for-9 down the stretch to pull away for its second straight win. Şengün led the Rockets with 23 points and added 11 rebounds and 11 assists for his 15th career triple-double - passing Hakeem Olajuwon for second in franchise history. "Hopefully I play with the Rockets for long, long years and pass James Harden," Şengün said. The former Houston guard leads the franchise with 46 career triple-doubles. "That's going to be my next goal." The Rockets recognized Şengün for his achievement and Durant for his - the latter received a game ball, Udoka said. "I try not to make it about myself in there. I understand that it's rare to hit these type of accomplishments and I don't ever want to undersell it," Durant said. "But we playing a team game and it's not about me most of the time." item.title: Jets Insider Says Mike Tomlin Could Be More Than a Pipe Dream
item.description: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty It’s Thanksgiving, and the New York Jets’ season is pretty much over. Sure, at 3-8, they’re not mathematically eliminated quite yet, but they have a better chance of finishing with the No. 1 overall pick than making the AFC Wildcard at this rate. Most fans likely have their minds set on the 2027 NFL Draft, where the Jets have three first-round picks, or free agency, when they’ll be flush with cap space. But arguably the most exciting thing for a lot of Jets fans will be the search for a new head coach if Aaron Glenn gets fired, and one long-time team insider seems to think New York will have a chance at landing a coach with Super Bowl-winning pedigree, Mike Tomlin. Jets Would Have a Chance at Mike Tomlin SNY’s Connor Hughes, who is one of the most plugged-in reporters on the New York Jets beat, seems to think the team would have a shot at hiring Tomlin if he wanted to throw his hat in the ring in the upcoming hiring cycle. “I think there might be something there with Tomlin where it’s the opportunity to come to New York, where (John) Harbaugh’s on the other side. Like they have a very good relationship, a competitive, like a very competitive, fiery relationship in a constructive way. I think he would actually be enticed by that,” Hughes said, about Tomlin potentially coming to New York. “If Woody (Johnson) gave him complete and full control, which I mean, he basically gave Aaron Glenn, so I have no idea why you wouldn’t give it to Tomlin, I could absolutely see a world where Woody’s willing to invest in Tomlin the way that he would have to, in order to convince him to leave that broadcasting gig.” "I think if Tomlin wants to coach again, the Jets will get a seat at the table to discuss it with him" @Connor_J_Hughes discusses the possibility of Mike Tomlin returning to coaching on the most recent episode of Jets Mailbag with @ChelseaSherrod pic.twitter.com/iAeOZK1Id1 — SNY Jets (@snyjets) November 21, 2026 “I think that if Tomlin wants to coach again, the Jets will get a seat at the table to discuss it with him.” For a team like the Jets, which has been looking for someone who can lift them out of the funk they’ve been in for nearly two decades, Tomlin may be their best bet. In 19 seasons with the Steelers, the Super Bowl champion head coach never had a losing season and accumulated a record of 193-114, one of the best in NFL history. If the Jets even thought they had a chance at him, they should stop at nothing to hire him. Jets Should Hand Over Full Control to Mike Tomlin It’s funny that Hughes brings up John Harbaugh when discussing Tomlin coming to the New York Jets, as Gang Green could try and pull out all the stops that the New York Giants did when hiring their head coach. Big Blue had their own general manager in place when hiring Harbaugh, Joe Schoen, similar to how Darren Mougey would likely remain with the Jets in the event that Glenn is fired. item.title: Bruins Postgame: A Wasted Spark, A ‘Disrespectful’ Start
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins got a spark, but they could not turn it into something they were thankful for. The Bruins (15-8-1) closed out the season series against the Winnipeg Jets (13-9-4) with a 4-2 loss on Wednesday night at TD Garden. Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten found the back of the net, and Jeremy Swayman made 14 saves in his seventh loss of the season. Read Next Bruins Grounded By Jets in Thanksgiving Eve Loss The Jets scored quickly, making it the sixth straight game where the Bruins have conceded the game’s first goal. Nikita Zadorov pinched as the puck rimmed around the boards, which sent the Jets down the ice. It took Kyle Connor 65 seconds to find the back of the net, doing so with Mark Scheifele and Josh Morrissey on a 3-on-1 against Will Borgen . “I think our stat is not pretty, especially the last few weeks when we don’t score the first goal. And again, it goes back to today,” Marco Sturm said postgame. “Just that turnover, and it ended up in the net, and all of a sudden, you chase the game again. We feel it, they feel it. So again, that’s something we definitely have to correct. And not even focus on scoring the first goal. Yes, we want to score the first goal, but also playing from behind and play that grinding game like we can, and not be pretty in the first five minutes, because that’s not who we are.” The Bruins chased for nearly the whole game. They did not hold a lead once on Wednesday night, and the game was tied for a combined 19:44, with the Jets holding a lead for the other 40:16. The Bruins responded to the Jets’ goal five minutes later, with Morgan Geekie scoring 11 seconds into their second power play of the night. And then Tanner Jeannot tilted the ice… or so we thought. Jeannot and Jets’ heavyweight Tyrel Bauer dropped the gloves for a spirited bout at center ice. Neither player got the takedown, but Jeannot pumped up an electrified TD Garden crowd after a minute-long fight. “It’s tough, obviously,” Geekie said. “We got it back pretty quick on the power play, and it’s one of those things that you get to kind of get the crowd back into it, and then Tanner does a hell of a job for us, obviously, and gets the place going. I just don’t think we took advantage of that. But yeah, it’s tough to play from behind in this league. It’s tough to play in this league in general, and teams are going to take advantage of that, and they kind of did. They got the momentum right away. We kind of tried to grab it back, but they’re a good team over there, and like I said, and just fell short of this one.” Read Next WATCH: Tanner Jeannot and Tyrel Bauer Engage in Heavyweight Bout Jeannot’s bout didn’t provide the Bruins with the momentum they sought, with Jeannot saying after the game that finding that spark was the purpose of the fight. item.title: Dak Prescott, Dallas Cowboys hoping for back-to-back wins for first time in 2026, stay playoff hunt
item.description: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) needs to continue hot streak and lead the his team to a win vs. the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday and notch first two-game win streak of the season to get to .500 at 6-6. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott is playing as well as any quarterback in NFL. The same can be said about Quinnen Williams and defensive tackle position and CeeDee Lamb at receiver. But none of it will truly matter if the Cowboys (5-6) don’t beat the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thursday in the annual Thanksgiving Day affair at AT&T Stadium, notch their first two-game win streak of the season and get back to .500 to stay in playoff contention. A loss would likely be final deathknell on what has been a disappointing start to the 2026 season. But the Cowboys remain hopeful because of a Prescott-led offense that ranks second in the NFL in scoring at 30.6 points per game, coming off back-to-back outings of 40 points in more. A 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers was followed by a 51-30 victory against the Tennessee Titans in what was the team’s best performance of the season. With 7 games left, the Cowboys are in officially in must-win, playoff mode from here on out to keep their fledgling hopes alive as they they are second in the NFC East behind the New York Giants (6-3-1). “Yeah, absolutely,” Prescott said when asked if the Cowboys were in playoff mode against the Eagles. “I mean, I think we put ourselves in that position a couple of weeks ago, frankly, right? Yeah, you said it — last week was, and this week is, and I would imagine every week going forward is, given how the division is.” It’s been a full calendar year since the Cowboys won back-to-back games. As well as they played last week, they have to find a way to keep it going against the Eaglees. “I spoke before about how big momentum is,” Prescott said. “And when you can grasp it and use it, and also write how tough it is when it’s against you, and right now, yeah, we’ve got it on our side. We’ve got to go make sure that we use it, and it’s not just me saying it, but we’ve gotta start fast and continue to build off of what we just did this past Sunday.” Said Lamb: “In order for us to get into the playoffs, we’ve got to win back-to-back games because, I mean, it’s what you need to do.” Prescott is the main source of optimism. The Cowboys haven’t lost to an NFC East team at home when Prescott is at quarterback since November 19, 2017 _ a span of 20 games. Prescott is currently playing the best football of his career with 668 passing yards and 10 total touchdowns against San Francisco and Tennessee the past two games. He has thrown for over 1,000 yards with 12 touchdowns and just one interception over his last three games. Prescott is currently second in the NFL in passing yards (3,049) and second in passing touchdowns (25). Is Prescott playing the best football of his career? “Sure,” Prescott said. “Because I do. item.title: Juventus vs Omonia – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Juventus vs Omonia – Predicted lineup and team news Juventus, currently fifth in the UEFA Europa League group table, take on Cypriot side Omonia Nicosia on Thursday at the Allianz Stadium in Turin. The Bianconeri come into tonight’s game in excellent form, having avoided defeat in their previous four matches across all competitions, with three wins and one draw. After beating Napoli 2-0 in Serie A and winning 2-1 away at AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League, Juventus drew 2-2 with Fiorentina before crushing Venezia 4-0 on Sunday. Under Luciano Spalletti, the Italian club have also gone unbeaten in their four Europa League fixtures this season, scoring an average of 1.9 goals per game. Juventus team news Spalletti has confirmed that he will rotate his squad ahead of Sunday’s Serie A meeting with Como. Goalkeeper Norberto Neto and young attacker Jeff Ekhator are both set to start for the first time this season, while Andrea Cambiaso comes back into the side on the left. Francisco Conceição is fit again after spending 40 days out with a shoulder problem, and Kerim Alajbegović may also return following a small injury picked up against Venezia. However, Juventus remain without a number of important players. Club captain Manuel Locatelli, Kenan Yıldız, Khéphren Thuram, Kamil Grabara, who has an ACL injury, Pierre Kalulu, who has a hamstring issue, and Nico González are all unavailable. Meanwhile, Daniele Rugani, Edon Zhegrova, and Arkadiusz Milik cannot feature tonight because they were left out of Juventus’s official UEFA Europa League squad. Juventus predicted lineup Possible Juventus starting XI: Neto; Gatti, Bremer, Lucumi; Weston McKennie, Douglas Luiz, Pape Matar Sarr, Andrea Cambiaso; Francisco Conceição, Jeff Ekhator, Jérémie Boga When will the match kick off? item.title: Why the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend could be doomed to fail
item.description: It is the season of feasting, of plates piled high, of over-indulgence in the name of festive excess and collective conviviality. How much is too much? That is a question that may well be answered on the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend, with a six-course tasting menu of global flavour whetting just about any appetite. The Twickenham grounds staff may not give thanks – even if there is a new pitch for the super-sized portions to be served – but for any rugby lover prone to immoderation, the larder is stocked for three days of gluttony. The world’s top 12 nations will take to the same surface in an ambitious array of Test matches that stretch from Friday afternoon to Sunday evening; this sport has not really known anything quite like it. All 12 teams will play at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham over three days on Nations Championship Finals weekend (Reuters) “It is amazing,” the South Africa rugby captain Siya Kolisi beamed at a chaotic launch on Wednesday as he looked ahead to a final with France. “It gives a different feeling for it because you know you’re fighting for something. Every game is important, but I think this has been really amazing because you’re competing against the north, but you’re also competing against the south in the same pools. “I think it has given it more drive and it has given it more excitement. I think it’s great to finally get that, the two best teams from the two hemispheres playing against each other.” Siya Kolisi is excited for the Nations Championship final (Getty) Will it be a success? The jury is out; so, too, are a significant number of potential match-goers. One can, if that way inclined and prepared to pay a pretty penny, still buy tickets to each and every day, with the top tier of the Allianz Stadium expected to be shut off entirely for Friday’s double-header. There may multiple mitigating factors, with England having just sold out three home games and fans elsewhere in Europe having had recent opportunity to watch their teams on home soil – but for a competition designed to grow the commercial potential of the sport, it is an inauspicious start. The format does not help matters, with fixtures only confirmed late last Saturday, hardly providing consumer certainty. The meaning of each contest could be said to be quite different, too: while England and New Zealand, say, can get excited for another tango, and South Africa and France dance again with a trophy on the line, Ireland and Wales may feel they have little to play for with their most significant results of November clearly in the rear-view mirror. Hopes in the future that it could become a destination event – Spain is known to be interested in hosting the finals in 2028 or 2030 – may rely on showing genuine supporter interest in each and every game. Frets over vulnerable fibres do not stop with the Twickenham turf, either, with the game’s top stars asked to stretch their sinews again at Test level. Those that are here, at least: Will Jordan an

item.title: Packers’ Micah Parsons unhappy after brutal no-show against Rams’ run game
item.description: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Packers’ Micah Parsons unhappy after brutal no-show against Rams’ run game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers took on the Los Angeles Rams to kick off Week 12 on Wednesday night. It was a matchup between two NFC playoff hopefuls on the night before Thanksgiving. For Micah Parsons and his teammates, it wasn’t a celebratory night. The Packers lost to the Rams on Wednesday night in Los Angeles. Quarterback Jordan Love threw two interceptions in this game. Meanwhile, Los Angeles ran the ball all over the field. Parsons shouldered the blame for this loss on Wednesday night. “If someone can line up 50 times and run it down your mouth and you don’t have an answer for it, that’s accountability,” he said, via ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) As he alluded to, Green Bay had no answer for the Rams run game. Los Angeles handed it off 47 times against the Packers on Wednesday. As a team, they ran for 241 yards. Blake Corum was the star of the show, though. The former Michigan star carried the ball 32 times, racking up 184 yards and a touchdown. He added two catches and 21 yards, giving him more than 200 yards from scrimmage. The Packers offense could not solve the Rams defense, either. They gained just 244 yards of offense on Wednesday. They were especially brutal on third down. Green Bay converted two of its eight third-down attempts. Green Bay has fallen to 6-5 on the 2026 campaign. This is going to set them back a bit in the NFC North standings. They are last place in the division, and are hoping to avoid finishing there at the end of the year. Green Bay will attempt to bounce back on December 6th when they take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 13. item.title: What channel is Lions vs. Bears on today? Time, TV schedule
item.description: First place in the NFC North will be on the line when the Detroit Lions host the Chicago Bears in their annual Thanksgiving Day game Thursday, Nov. 26, at Ford Field. The Lions (8-2) have won six consecutive games, the longest active winning streak in the NFL, after defeating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , 31-21, on Sunday. Jared Goff completed 20 of 28 passes for 279 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, while running back Jahmyr Gibbs scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns. Detroit's defense has held each of its past six opponents to 21 points or fewer. The Lions recorded four sacks against Tampa Bay in their first game since losing All-Pro edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending knee injury. More: Lions lose another defensive lineman for season with knee injury The Bears (8-2) have won five consecutive games under former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, including a 21-13 victory over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. Chicago hasn't trailed in any of its past five games. Johnson led the Bears to an NFC North championship last season, his first as Chicago's head coach, but lost both games against the Lions. Detroit has won four consecutive meetings against Chicago. Thursday marks the 87th Thanksgiving Day game for the Lions and their 21st against the Bears. The teams will also meet Jan. 3 at Soldier Field in Chicago. Here's how to watch Lions vs. Bears in Week 12 of the NFL season: What TV channel is Lions vs. Bears on today? TV: CBS (WWJ-TV, Channel 62, in Detroit) Streaming: Paramount+; NFL+ on eligible mobile devices Radio: 97.1 FM The Ticket in Detroit; Detroit Lions Radio Network Jim Nantz will handle play-by-play for CBS, with J.J. Watt as analyst and Tracy Wolfson reporting from the sidelines. Dan Miller will have the Lions radio call alongside analyst Lomas Brown. Lions vs. Bears start time today Kickoff: 1 p.m. ET Thursday, Nov. 26 Where: Ford Field, Detroit Records: Detroit 8-2, Chicago 8-2 The Lions' Thanksgiving Day tradition dates to 1934, when Detroit hosted Chicago in a game the Bears won, 19-16. The Lions have played annually on the holiday since 1945. Detroit defeated Chicago, 23-20, in the teams' most recent Thanksgiving Day meeting in 2024, snapping a seven-game holiday losing streak. The Bears hold an 11-9 advantage in Thanksgiving Day meetings. The Lions and Bears will open the NFL's Thanksgiving tripleheader, followed by the Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys at 4:30 p.m. on FOX and the Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills at 8:20 p.m. on NBC. Lions vs. Bears football odds Line: Chicago by 2½ Over/under: 55½ Moneyline: Chicago -140, Detroit +115 The Bears were 2½-point favorites, according to BetMGM. Betting lines are subject to change. item.description: Juventus vs Omonia – Match preview and team news Juventus, sitting in fifth place in the UEFA Europa League group standings, will face Omonia from Cyprus on Thursday in their next match at the Allianz Stadium in Torino. item.title: Dangote Refinery shares to trade on NGX December 1
item.description: Shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) on December 1, the company has announced. Devakumar Edwin, Vice-President, Oil and Gas, Dangote Group, disclosed the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing will follow the refinery’s initial public offering (IPO), which attracted significant investor interest and was heavily oversubscribed. The development comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s plan to allocate shares to investors, paving the way for the completion of the offer and its stock market debut. Dangote Refinery had sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong demand from investors. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, President of Dangote Industries Limited, said the refinery planned to list on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, the industrialist said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and other parts of the world. item.title: Registered Voters Now 100m As INEC Removes 1.6m Invalid Records
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The update comes as the Commission said it has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. According to him, the Commission removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register – the removal has now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were taken off the list, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. “Beyond hardware and logistics, we must also account for inclusivity and evidentiary clarity. Following three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) that added over 10.77 million new registrants and an ABIS and statutory claims-and-objections audit that purged over 1.6 million invalid, duplicate, or deceased records, our verified register stands at over 100 million citizens, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) requiring accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were an additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. He said that although INEC had previously stood down its broader revalidation exercise until after the elections, the commission resolved to immediately address serious infractions identified on the old register. “So, consequent upon that, the ICT department, working with the Voter Registry, have been able to complete the validation of those that contain duplications only, and those we had some form of stroke registrations. “In other words, those places where

item.title: The defence tech revolution is changing how we innovate
item.description: Cpl Aaron J Stone/UK Ministry of Defence Only five years ago, defence technology start-ups had little choice but to wait for government funding to build and test their inventions – often in complex, multi-year programmes. No longer, however: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has prompted such a fast, furious response that military innovation timescales have shrunk dramatically. “Ukraine is becoming a real-world lab for military innovation, and it’s innovating at a pace greater than anything that we’ve seen previously,” says Ola Fashade, an air vice-marshal in the Royal Air Force and director of military digitalisation and the rapid AI delivery task force at the UK’s Ministry of Defence (MoD). “Agility and tempo of adaptation is critical. In a contested battlespace, technology that works well on day one, by day eight has become a little muted – and by day twelve it’s probably no longer relevant. And if you don’t adapt over that period, what you have is a very expensive and ineffective bag of steel.” Advertisement That raises the question of how significant this accelerated innovation could become. In September 2026, New Scientist CoLab, sponsored by BAE Systems, brought together leading thinkers and investors from industry, the military and academia to discuss the factors driving this innovation and the lessons that can be transferred to other industries. Staying alive The investment for this step change is coming both from the technology incubators based within military prime contractors – like the Launchpad incubator at BAE Systems – and from a host of venture capital (VC) companies worldwide. “The idea behind Launchpad is to forge an ecosystem that gets technology from defence start-ups into the front line quicker, or into spinouts, before they run out of money and die,” says David Ewing, head of technology commercialisation at BAE Systems. In addition, VC funding is seeing a raft of new multibillion-dollar military tech players, dubbed neoprimes, that complement the work of the primes on bigger-ticket battlespace items. The poster child for the neoprimes, says Samuel Burrell, a partner at the pan-European VC firm Expeditions Fund, is the nascent British air defence start-up Cambridge Aerospace, which reached a valuation of $3.4 billion with little but a convincing tech narrative: “They had no battlefield data, no product – just a compelling team and an idea on paper.” It wasn’t all talk: Cambridge Aerospace has begun delivering its Skyhammer air defence missile for taking out Shahed-type drones and cruise missiles. A solid-rocket-motor-powered ballistic missile interceptor, Starhammer, will ship in 2027. In the maritime battlespace, meanwhile, fast-scaling neoprime Kraken Technology Group of Hampshire, UK, has raised $175 million from various VC firms, valuing it at $1 billion, to further develop its uncrewed surface vessel and drone technologies for users including the MoD, NATO and the US Special Operations Command. item.title: Rewane projects 4.5% growth, urges investors to rethink strategies
item.description: By Onome Onyeme The Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, has projected Nigeria’s economic growth at between 4.3 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, urging investors to rethink traditional investment strategies and embrace emerging opportunities. Speaking at the 23rd edition of the Alpha Morgan Economic Review, held virtually yesterday, Rewane said changing economic realities, technological innovation and evolving business models were reshaping investment decisions globally. “The rules of the past are no longer the rules of the present, definitely not the rules of the future,” he said, urging investors to embrace innovation, research and emerging industries rather than rely on past market performance. Rewane, who examined global economic developments and Nigeria’s investment outlook, said businesses and investors that failed to adapt to changing realities risked losing relevance. He cited the evolution of global businesses, including Apple, as examples of how innovation and leadership could determine corporate fortunes, stressing that past success was no guarantee of future dominance. Rewane observed increasing participation in the capital market, with more companies raising funds through the market rather than relying solely on commercial bank loans. However, he warned of possible property market bubble risks, particularly amid the rapid expansion of construction and property investments in Lagos. Rewane projected that some companies could record revenue growth of between 25 and 40 per cent, driven by capital investment, expansion and increased operations across Africa. He also projected the Naira to trade between N1,500 and N1,600 per dollar in 2027, while anticipating an end to global interest rate increases. He clarified that the projections represented his personal assessment of economic developments. item.title: Five things to expect in 2027
item.description: Things are set to heat up in 2027. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And these impacts will hit as farmers are already struggling with higher prices linked to the war in Iran, and with international aid reduced around the world. Democrats and Trump The Democratic takeover of both chambers of the US Congress in January promises to transform the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, giving his opponents powerful tools to challenge his agenda — but not a free hand to impose their own. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. Perhaps the more immediate impact will come from congressional investigations. Democratic-led committees can subpoena officials and demand documents on alleged corruption, Trump’s family business dealings, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Such scrutiny could trigger lengthy court battles. Democrats could also pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although removing him would require a two-thirds Senate majority — a formidable hurdle. In the Senate, Democrats can block Trump’s cabinet and judicial appointments, including any Supreme Court nominee. But most legislation needs 60 Senate votes to overcome procedural obstruction, and Trump can veto measures that reach his desk. Overriding him requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers. The result could be two years of subpoenas, spending standoffs and confrontation, punctuated by possible deals on shared priorities. French presidential election After 10 years in power, Emmanuel Macron will step down following France’s presidential election, scheduled for April 18 and May 2. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: CBN raises BDC’s dollar cash limit to $1m weekly
item.description: Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. item.title: Uduere: ‘Their sacrifices won’t be in vain’ – Obi, Kwankwaso visit slain NDC members’ families
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume, Henry Umoru & Egufe Yafugborhi Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, has condemned the killings at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State during Monday’s rally of the party, describing the incident as tragic and unacceptable. Meanwhile, Omo-Agege has criticised the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue of the rally, alleging that about 50 officers failed to protect members of the party during the attack. Also, the Obidient Movement condemned Monday’s attack, observing that Nigerians can no longer have confidence in a police force that appears more interested in protecting political interests than protecting citizens, stressing that the police derive their authority from the people. Obi said it was disturbing that some people could resort to killing others simply because they want to occupy political positions, assuring the bereaved families that the sacrifices of the victims would not be in vain. “People cannot sacrifice for this in vain. All the sacrifices will not be in vain. We cannot kill or harm people simply because we want to become political leaders,” he said. Obi spoke, Tuesday, night during a condolence visit to the family of the late Moses Anaughe, who was shot dead during the attack. Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly representing Ughelli North Constituency I and former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission, was attacked by the assailants while stepping out of his vehicle. He was allegedly shot at close range. At the deceased’s residence in Agbarho, Obi consoled his widow and was seen sharing playful moments with their young son in an effort to comfort the grieving family. He was accompanied by the NDC governorship candidate in Delta State, Deacon Oyovwaiye Chris, and the party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Police came to watch me being executed — Omo-Agege Meanwhile, Omo-Agege expressed disappointment that despite the heavy police presence, the assailants were able to unleash violence on the gathering. He said: “We went to the campaign event with six trucks of policemen deployed to the venue. “We expected protection for everyone at the venue. It never occurred to us that they were merely coming principally to watch me being executed.” Obi, Kwankwaso visit Umukoro’s family The NDC presidential candidate, yesterday, continued his condolence visits alongside his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, with a visit to the family of slain activist in Abraka, Ethiope East Local Government Area of the state, Efemena Umukoro, who was also killed during the party’s campaign rally at Uduere. They were received by the widow, Mrs. Gift Umukoro, and other members of the family. item.title: NLC, TUC feud: How we brokered peace in Ajaero, Osifo’s rift — Obiajulu
item.description: *lSays some individuals exploited situation to tear labour movement apart By Victor Ahiuma-Young The protracted disagreement between the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport relief agreement with the NLC, which the TUC rejected, threatened to undermine the unity and collective bargaining strength of organised labour. The disagreement escalated into public exchanges and personal attacks between NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, raising concerns that the welfare and interests of Nigerian workers were being overshadowed by the leadership crisis. Worried that the feud could further divide the labour movement and weaken its ability to defend workers’ interests, veteran labour leaders, led by pioneer NLC President, Hassan Sunmonu, intervened and brokered peace between the two leaders. Other prominent figures involved in the reconciliation included Dr Peace Obiajulu, Comrades Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. In this interview, former TUC President, Dr Obiajulu, recounts what triggered the crisis, how it escalated, and how the intervention of the labour elders helped restore cordial relations between the two labour centres. She reveals that poor communication largely fuelled the disagreement, while some individuals exploited the situation, warning that the crisis nearly tore the labour movement apart and ultimately put workers’ interests at risk. What actually led to the disagreement between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress, and how did you get involved in the reconciliation? To start with, I was not even aware that there was a disagreement between the two organisations. I was called by Quadri Olaleye, a former President of TUC. He told me that the President of NLC had asked whether Mrs Obiajulu, whom we fondly call Mummy, had been informed about the meeting. That was when I asked whether there was a problem between TUC and NLC. He said yes. I responded that it was a family matter, just like disagreements between a husband and wife or among children in a family. In all honesty, I do not know who initiated the reconciliation process. I am sure it was the elders. They must have seen what was happening on television and read about it in the newspapers. If I had come across the situation myself, I would equally have reached out to some of the elders to intervene. I would not like to see organised labour become a target of public ridicule. The moment TUC and NLC begin to quarrel or fall apart, workers are left on their own. Whenever there is a problem within the labour movement, workers are the ones who suffer because nobody will be left to speak effectively on their behalf. How serious had the disagreement become before the elders intervened? If there is a disagreement between NLC and TUC, workers ultimately bear the consequences. item.title: Risk of retaining fuel subsidy outweighed political consequences – Idris
item.description: • President misrepresented on electricity supply promise – Onanuga •FG defends power sector reforms, increased revenue to states By Juliet Umeh MINISTER of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the removal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates saved Nigeria from imminent economic collapse. Idris, who spoke at an interactive session with journalists organised by the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council Media and Strategic Communications team in Lagos, Monday, said the President took politically risky decisions in the overriding interest of the country. He maintained that the reforms had improved government revenues at all levels, strengthened the economy and positioned the country for sustainable growth. He said: “When the President took office in May 2023, there were two major policy decisions. One was doing away with this monster called fuel subsidy. The second was ensuring that the multiple exchange rate regimes that we had in this country were also done away with. “Presidents after presidents, everyone knew that fuel subsidy was a big problem and a big drain on the economy of this country. But no one was able to achieve its removal until President Bola Tinubu came. “It was not a convenient decision for Mr President. In fact, it was politically risky for him, for someone who had just won an election, who had just been sworn in and who had another election staring him in the face.” Idris explained that the administration considered the consequences of retaining the subsidy and concluded that delaying the reforms would have been more damaging to the country. “The risk of waiting any longer far outweighed whatever political risk he, as a person, as a president or as a politician, should take. “This created enough fiscal headroom, not just for the Federal Government but also for the sub-nationals. Federal Government has made a lot more money. Sub-nationals have made a lot more money,” he said. Economy on path to recovery The minister also said international financial institutions and rating agencies had acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s economic outlook. He said: “The IMF, the World Bank, everybody is saying, yes, we have some challenges as a nation, but our economy is on the path that will lead us to prosperity. “Our GDP is on the rise. Inflation that was becoming a big problem has been curtailed. Headline inflation, food inflation, all are down.” However, journalists at the meeting raised concerns over persistent insecurity, high petrol prices, inadequate electricity supply, distribution of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and the impact of increased allocations to state governments on citizens’ welfare. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 26 – Eye in the Sky: The Milky Way over Lençóis
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 26 – Eye… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Eye in the Sky: The Milky Way over Lençóis Explanation: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. And there is much to behold in today’s featured image . The Milky Way shines bright in the sky of Brazil , over the white sand dunes and dark lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park . We can see different parts of the Milky Way as it apparently rotates in the sky every night and throughout the year. This composite image was taken later in the night in July from a latitude of approximately 2º south. It shows some prominent Milky Way features, such as dark dust lanes and colorful nebulas . But does the Galaxy really appear arched like a rainbow in the sky? No, this is an artifact of a picture taken with a wide-angle lens. As the Galaxy was artfully framed by the photographer, it matches the contour of the dark lagoon creating the illusion of a cosmic eye , half in space and half on the ground. Is this eye in the sky looking back at you? Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? item.title: Tinubu vows to sustain peace, defeat insurgency in North-East
item.description: •Promises rescue of abducted Askira Uba schoolchildren •Shettima, Zulum hail security gains, seek second term for Tinubu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has pledged to sustain the relative peace recorded in Borno State and the North-East, directing security agencies to intensify operations against fleeing insurgents. Tinubu, who spoke yesterday at an All Progressives Congress, APC, rally in Maiduguri ahead of the 2027 general elections, said the security gains achieved by the armed forces would be consolidated and translated into full economic recovery. In a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, the President commended Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Zulum, for restoring hope and transforming the state’s economy. “Let me start by thanking the Governor of the State, Prof. Babagana Zulum. Well done on restoring Borno State and transforming its economy. “You restored our hope by believing that stability will bring development,” he said. Tinubu, who commissioned projects including the National Youth Service Corps Female Lodge and Borno International Conference Centre, said the North-East had witnessed economic improvements in the last three years, with increased investments in education, healthcare and infrastructure. He urged fleeing insurgents to surrender their weapons, assuring troops of continued government support and improved welfare for them and their families. On the abducted schoolchildren from Askira Uba, the President promised intensified intelligence gathering and rescue operations. “I think there’s a point to note here: the abducted children of Askira Uba School. They are there, and with our prayers and intelligence, our armed forces will rescue them, Insha Allah,” he said. Attributing the security gains to cooperation among political leaders, residents, the Federal Government and security agencies, Tinubu thanked the people of Borno for their support and commended Vice-President Kashim Shettima for his loyalty. He also acknowledged former governor Ali Modu Sheriff and other North-East political leaders for their contributions. In his remarks, Shettima urged voters to reject the former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, questioning his leadership capacity. “You don’t expect someone who could not provide leadership at home by reconciling his own people to provide leadership at a national level,” he said. Shettima urged the electorate to reward Tinubu’s administration with a second term, claiming it had performed well in Borno, Bauchi, Taraba, Adamawa and other states. Earlier, Zulum thanked Tinubu for his interventions in Borno, saying they had contributed to the state’s recovery and economic repositioning. “If someone has done well for you, like our President, then we should give him a good reward. “We have witnessed relative peace in Borno State and the North-East,” he said. item.title: Seeking Refuge on Resolution Island
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Seeking Refuge on Resolution… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the late 1800s, wildlife conservationists in New Zealand were recognizing how predators such as stoats , brought to the country to control other nonnative animal populations, were becoming a threat to native birds. Naturalists at the time surmised that some of the nation’s islands could serve as sanctuaries where endemic species could persist, free from the voracious newcomers. Resolution Island, located in the Fiordland region along the rugged southwest edge of New Zealand’s South Island, was one of the first eyed for this purpose. Conservationist Thomas Henry Potts proposed in 1872 that the island could be a place where “wingless species, and birds of feeble powers of flight, might there find a refuge for some of their representatives.” So began an early systematic effort to protect kiwi, kākāpō , and other native birds on Resolution Island, the largest of the approximately 90 islands in Fiordland National Park . This image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on December 12, 2025, shows the island’s setting amid a landscape of steep-sided valleys carved by glaciers and now inundated by the ocean. The uninhabited island rises from sea level to the summit of Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters (3,507 feet). Its diverse habitats and vegetation communities range from bogs and wetlands near the coast to widespread podocarp forests at middle elevations to tussock grasslands in the subalpine and alpine areas. Offshore, the Taumoana (Five Fingers Peninsula) Marine Reserve protects estuarine and wave-exposed rocky reef habitats at the entrance to Dusky Sound, east of Five Fingers Peninsula. Farther into the sound, Pigeon Island was the onetime home of Richard Henry, who was named caretaker of Resolution Island after it was designated a reserve in 1891. In what some have called a “ landmark effort ,” Henry spent years transporting more than 700 birds, mostly kiwi and kākāpō, by rowboat to Resolution and other would-be island sanctuaries nearby. In 1900, however, people began spotting mustelids on Resolution. It turns out the island is within swimming distance for animals such as stoats. Henry was intent on trapping the interlopers but eventually abandoned the project and moved on to caretaking work on another island. The spirit of his efforts lives on, though. A Department of Conservation program started in 2008 aims to control stoat populations and bolster native species on Resolution. item.title: 10 Classic Books Worth Reading Over and Over
item.description: Most of us treat classic literature like a checklist to conquer in high school or college and then never touch those books again. You power through the plot, underline a few quotes for a term paper, and move on to whatever else is new. The catch is that great books rarely reveal their most fascinating tricks on the first pass. When you already know the ending, your brain stops racing for answers and begins to notice the machinery holding all those mysteries and themes together. Suddenly, an unreliable narrator's sleight of hand becomes obvious, or a throwaway line in chapter two hits like a freight train in light of later developments .

item.title: Registered voters now 100m, says Amupitan, INEC Chairman
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, says it has removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Amupitan said that the removal had now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were purged, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. He said that although INEC had previously stood down its broader revalidation exercise until after the elections, the commission resolved to immediately address serious infractions identified on the old register. “So, consequent upon that, the ICT department, working with the Voter Registry, have been able to complete the validation of those that contain duplications only, and those we had some form of stroke registrations. “In other words, those places where you have BBBB, AAAA, CCCC without complete names, we felt that those ones are too serious to be left on the old register. “So, where you also have duplication, one name, same picture, having five registrations, we have also addressed all those numbers. “By the time we are putting the verified and clean-up register together, the national voters’ register is reduced from 103 million to 100 million,’’ Amupitan said. He promised that details would be released as soon as the final figure was out. Vanguard News The post Registered voters now 100m, says Amupitan, INEC Chairman appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu, Peter Obi, Soludo, others mourn as Nollywood legend, Pete Edochie dies at 79
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi, Benjamin Njoku, Vincent Ujumadu & Johnbosco Agbakwuru PRESIDENT Bola Ahmed Tinubu, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, and Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, have expressed deep sadness over the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing his passing as a monumental loss to his community, the Igbo nation, Nigeria and Africa. In separate condolence messages, they described Edochie as a distinguished son of Anambra State and one of Africa’s most celebrated actors, whose exceptional talent and contribution to the creative industry projected African culture and traditions to audiences across the world. Nigeria has lost one of its greatest thespians —Tinubu In a tribute personally signed by him, the President described Edochie, popularly known as Ebube Dike, as a graceful and larger-than-life personality, both on and off the screen. The tribute read: “It was with deep sorrow that I received the news of the passing of Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie, better known as Pete Edochie. “Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor and one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on screen and in person. “He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter and charm to many homes. “I recall his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s evergreen novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s, and his many brilliant performances afterwards. “Through memorable performances in productions such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, he helped shape the evolution and international visibility of Nollywood. “His portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values and the complexities of human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide.” Tinubu added:”Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster and journalist — truly one of our finest. “His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms and popular culture remains indisputable. “As I mourn the passing of this legendary actor, I also reflect on his life. Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully. “In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather.” Obi pays tribute In his condolence message, Obi recalled Edochie’s memorable portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, noting that the actor’s deep understanding of African culture and command of both English and Igbo distinguished him as an exceptional performer. item.title: Thugs attack NDC convoy, campaign office in Benin; ‘We don’t support violence’ – APC
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Omeiza Ajayi Ozioruva Aliu & Gift ChapiOdekina Benin City — Political thugs allegedly attacked the convoy and campaign office of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Benin, Edo State, yesterday, barely 72 hours after some members of the party were killed at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State on Monday. Six persons, including supporters of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, were killed in the attack. This is even as the national leadership of the party also yesterday raised alarm that the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government was pushing the opposition out of the political space, following escalating cases of political thuggery, attacks and violence. The NDC said it received an intelligence report on a possible attack at its town hall meeting in Benin, where its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, was expected to address supporters. Edo State Coordinator of the party’s campaign council, John Yakubu, who confirmed the attack, said the party had been informed of plans to disrupt the event, as members prepared to leave their campaign office to receive Obi at the airport. He said, despite the intelligence report, the party went ahead with plans to welcome Obi, while calling attention to the need for security around the event. Videos seen by our correspondent showed blood stains on the party’s convoys, including bullet exhibits seen on the floor of the party’s campaign office. Surrounded by other supporters and hospital personnel, a man was seen in the video to have been covered in a pool of his blood, and was seen being attended to at an unknown hospital. Police confirm shooting as Obi, NDC hold townhall meeting Vanguard also learned that a yet-to-be-identified person reportedly shot at an NDC branded vehicle, injuring one as police said they had launched a manhunt for him. The incident happened when NDC supporters lined Airport Road to welcome the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his entourage into the Edo State capital for a twin hall meeting. The suspects, three in number, were said to have arrived the scene in a black Toyota Hilux vehicle. Confirming the incident, the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, of the Edo State police command, Eno Ikoedem, said the suspects, “upon sighting police operatives stationed at the airport exit gate, unable to proceed, made a U-turn and opened fire on persons at the scene before fleeing.” She said: “During the attack, one Aimionkhale Micheal ‘m’ sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was immediately rushed to the hospital, where he is currently receiving medical attention.” The PPRO said the Commissioner of Police, CP Patrick Daaor, immediately visited the scene and was subsequently at the hospital to assess the condition of the victim. item.title: 2027: No margin for error, INEC warns RECs, sets 6 operational priorities
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has told Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs that “margin for error simply does not exist” in the conduct of the 2027 General Elections. This was as he set six operational priorities for the RECs, from whom he said he expects “immediate, documented compliance and personal accountability.” Amupitan spoke on Wednesday in Abuja at a strategic consultative meeting with the RECs from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. Reviewing the off-cycle elections since he assumed office in October 2025, Amupitan said the exercises showed “what is achievable when planning starts early, logistics are properly sequenced, and supervision is hands-on.” They covered the governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, the FCT Area Council elections and sixteen legislative bye-elections. He said every bottleneck identified in the off-cycle reviews “must be permanently closed before Saturday’s nationwide simulation and well ahead of January 16.” He cautioned that “general elections operate on an entirely different magnitude and complexity.” The Commission, he said, is managing a verified register of over 100 million voters, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities who need accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “In an exercise of that scale, even minor administrative lapses in one state can trigger national headlines and cast doubt on otherwise solid work elsewhere. Margin for error simply does not exist. At this decisive stage of the electoral cycle, the calendar no longer allows for leisurely deliberation or deferred action,” he said. According to him, the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 177,299 polling units, followed on Saturday, February 6, 2027, by the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly polls. He described the RECs as “the Commission’s chief operational commanders in the field,” adding that the credibility and public legitimacy of the elections “rest squarely on the precision, vigilance, institutional neutrality, and administrative rigour” with which they lead their state offices. The first priority, he said, is the nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, in two polling units per ward. “It is a live operational stress test of our upgraded BVAS devices, our logistics workflows, and our automated result validation safeguards on the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” he said, referring to the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). Every REC, he said, must personally oversee state-level preparations and submit “a comprehensive, candid technical audit” to INEC Headquarters by Monday, November 30, 2026. item.title: India’s government ponders cradle to grave AI oversight
item.description: Indian politicians have proposed that AI could take a major role in citizens’ lives, partly through pervasive surveillance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week spelled out his vision for an AI-based app that would collect data about children as they grow and analyze it to determine their aptitude for different types of study or careers. Modi suggested that parents of three-year-old children should enter data about their offspring’s activities and accomplishments into a government-run system that is also accessible to teachers and even a child’s friends. Those records, the PM suggested, will “help identify children's interests and aptitude from an early age and redirect them in the study of their choice in future.” That’s not an entirely creepy idea, because gaining access to India’s top tertiary institutions requires students to pay a hefty fee to sit for entrance exams. Modi pitched recommendations from the AI-powered app as something parents will appreciate as they contemplate whether to fund their offspring’s studies. India’s most populous state, Uttar Pradesh (UP), has proposed to build an “AI Stack” to serve its 240 million-plus residents. A 178-page tender seeks bidders to build a system that uses the state’s Family ID – a unique identifier for each household – to link data held by multiple agencies so it can be put to work in a dozen AI use cases. One of those use cases is a tool for “AI-Enabled Social Media Monitoring and Urban Grievance Detection” that “analyses publicly available social media content including online news channels and connected grievance channels to detect emerging urban issues, citizen complaints, service interruptions, and recurring service gaps.” The government wants that system to autonomously route complaints to relevant agencies, to automate actions like sending crews to patch up damaged roads. Critics have pointed to vague wording in the tender as potentially allowing the UP government to link this system to other agencies – a matter of concern given Indian state and national governments have implemented internet shutdowns to stop protestors from communicating on social media services and messaging apps. Another use case is a knowledge assistant for state police that looks up case histories and other data but can’t use it to assess evidence or provide investigative conclusions. An app for teachers will advise them on how to create custom content to meet students’ needs. Healthcare workers would also get an app to help them make recommendations during patient visits. Citizens get natural language interfaces to a system that offers advice on how to identify and access government services and schemes. UP wants to drive these apps with self-hosted open-weight models, and to use only anonymized datasets. India’s Internet Freedom Foundation worries that the systems described in the tender aren’t explicitly authorized by any legislation, and that the document doesn’t mention important oversight measures for the AI St

item.title: The sky was once full of stars, kids; then the FCC let Elon Musk launch a million datacenter satellites
item.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. Down on Earth, meanwhile, scientists trying to observe the universe continue to bemoan the obstructions caused by mega-constellations of broadband-beamin

item.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
item.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. Read full article Comments

item.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
item.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. The table below details moonrise timings for a selection of cities spread across the globe for Dec. 23-24: Local moonrise timings for the December 2026 full Cold Moon City Local time New York 3:58 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 London 4:07 p.m. GMT on Dec. 24 Tokyo 4:32 p.m. JST on Dec. 24 Beijing 4:55 p.m. CST on Dec. 24 Sydney 8:36 p.m. AEDT on Dec. 24 Why it's called the Cold Moon The December full moon is often called the Cold Moon in reference to the often freezing temperatures that can descend this time of the year. It's also known as the " Long Night Moon " by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", according to Time and Date , while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees.
